taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce serpens is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Tiny smooth creeping mat with very small rounded opposite leaves and stems that often hug the soil closely.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew treats Chamaesyce serpens as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia serpens, native in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
best_field_traits: tiny rounded to oval opposite leaves
often roots or closely hugs nodes against soil
morphology_keys.comparison_training: This is the tiniest, smoothest mat in B109. E. prostrata is coarser and often hairy; E. villifera is conspicuously hairy.
